plan.change: Phase C3-2 Trusted Static Evidence with exact-blob trusted Change OS contracts.
expectedChanges: Add a base-owned data-only Trusted Static Check Registry whose initial IDs are change-operations-regression and node-syntax and which contains no candidate command or script fields.

Represent change-operations-regression as exact Git blob contracts for security-critical Change OS workflow/tool files, including mode/type, so comments, dead strings, parser differences, partial edits, and hidden behavior changes cannot preserve PASS.

Use a two-stage authorization model for future contracted-file changes: a registry-only authorization PR takes effect only after merge, and a later fresh PR may change a contracted file to the preauthorized blob; the candidate registry never authorizes its own PR.

Add a base-owned Trusted Static Check Executor that validates the immutable Plan, repository, exact base/target SHA, base-owned registry blob, base-owned Risk Policy blob, and base-owned executor provenance before evaluating candidate Git data.

Execute node-syntax only through a fixed base-owned parse-only executor over safe temporary files generated from applicable exact candidate Git blobs; never execute candidate modules, tests, workflows, Plan commands, or candidate-provided executor definitions.

Reject unknown static check IDs explicitly, record trusted non-applicability as N/A rather than PASS, and ensure every requested check yields exactly one result so partial execution cannot produce static success.

Extend the existing base-owned Change Verification Evidence job to emit a separate run/attempt-unique trusted Static Evidence artifact and make static failure fail the same ruleset-required trusted-mechanical-evidence job.

Record repository, exact base/target SHA, Plan Lock identity, actor/triggering actor, run ID/attempt, workflow ref/SHA, registry/executor/Risk Policy source blobs, check ID, definition version, executor kind, applicability, result, exit code, and contract evidence.
Keep verificationState UNVERIFIED and leave authenticated human attestation, Verification Record v0.3 final integration, VERIFIED promotion, Phase D/E, and production out of scope.
Add regression/adversarial tests and update Change Plan, Verification, and Operations documentation.
hqDecisions: C3-2 adds trusted static evidence only; authenticated human attestation and final VERIFIED remain out of scope.
Candidate Plan values select only registry IDs and cannot provide commands, script paths, shell fragments, executor kinds, trusted expected blobs, or runtime overrides.
Security-critical Change OS contracts use exact Git blob identity rather than substring or custom YAML-semantic parsing.
The current PR always uses registry/executor/Risk Policy from github.event.pull_request.base.sha; candidate definitions cannot authorize their own changes.
Future contracted-file changes require two separate merges: base-owned registry authorization first, then the preauthorized file change.
The existing ruleset-required trusted-mechanical-evidence job remains the enforcement carrier so no new unprotected status-check name is introduced.

plan.manualCheckExemptionReason: C3-2 is a staging Change OS trust-boundary implementation. Pre-merge evidence is C3-1 trusted gates plus regression/review; post-merge canaries exercise the newly trusted static executor. Authenticated human attestation is C3-3.
plan.rollback: Revert the C3-2 staging merge as one Change OS package if post-merge canaries reveal a trust-boundary defect. Do not modify production.
outOfScope: Executing candidate-controlled application code, test code, workflow code, shell commands, or Plan-provided commands
Custom YAML semantic parsing as a trusted security boundary
Registering release-validator before a safe data-only trusted definition exists
unverified: Final VERIFIED remains unavailable because authenticated human attestation and final evidence integration are intentionally not implemented in C3-2.
plan.problem: Plan.staticChecks are declarations only. The aborted PR #51 also showed that substring-based workflow contracts are spoofable, while PR #56 showed that custom YAML semantic parsing would unnecessarily expand the trusted parser surface.
plan.currentContract: C3-1 provides base-owned pull_request_target mechanical evidence for immutable Plan Lock, Scope, Risk, and Impact and leaves verificationState UNVERIFIED. Risk Policy already derives static-check applicability from changed paths.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: A candidate can name a static check without trusted execution provenance. Trusted static workflow evidence must also be immune to comments, dead strings, parser interpretation gaps, stale SHA reuse, and candidate definition overrides.
plan.design: Create a data-only base-owned registry. change-operations-regression contains exact expected Git blob/mode/type contracts for security-critical Change OS files. node-syntax selects only a fixed base-owned parse-only executor. The trusted executor validates the locked Plan and exact candidate SHA, verifies that the loaded registry and Risk Policy bytes match their PR-base Git blobs, reads candidate content through Git object identity, compares contracted files by exact blob identity, and syntax-checks applicable JavaScript from safe generated temporary files. The workflow invokes only trusted-base code, captures machine JSON privately, uploads a separate Static Evidence artifact, and includes the static exit code in the existing required job's final decision.
alternativesRejected: Execute command strings or script paths from Plan.staticChecks; this creates direct candidate-controlled execution.
Run candidate tests or Change OS modules inside pull_request_target; fixed paths still execute candidate-controlled code.
Use substring presence for workflow contracts; comments and dead strings can spoof trusted PASS.
Use a custom YAML semantic parser as the trust root; parser-versus-GitHub interpretation drift creates a new bypass surface.
Duplicate check ID to command mappings inside workflow YAML; this creates workflow/registry drift.
Treat unknown IDs as SKIP/PASS or trusted N/A as PASS; this falsifies execution evidence.
Allow a candidate registry to authorize contracted files in the same PR; trusted definitions must come from the PR base.
Register release-validator now; its current implementation may execute candidate repository JavaScript and needs a separate safe trusted definition.
plan.migration: Historical Plan Locks and Verification Records are not rewritten. PR #51 and PR #56 remain closed and unmerged. The C3-2 implementation PR is bootstrapped by C3-1 because the new static executor is not yet present on its base. After C3-2 merges, future registry updates may authorize a later contracted-file blob but cannot authorize a same-PR file change because execution always uses the base-owned registry.
plan.compatibility: The ruleset continues to require plan-risk-gate and trusted-mechanical-evidence. C3-2 extends the latter job to include static gating while retaining C3-1 mechanical evidence as a separate artifact. Existing high-risk static check IDs remain change-operations-regression and node-syntax.
boundaryCases: Unknown command-like ID such as node evil.js produces explicit FAIL and no command execution.
Candidate modifications to registry/executor/Risk Policy cannot affect the current PR trusted run because those sources are loaded from the exact PR base.
Candidate modification to a contracted workflow/tool fails unless its exact blob was authorized by an earlier merged base registry.
Changing a contracted file while changing its expected blob in the same candidate registry still fails because the current run uses the base registry.
Comments, dead strings, YAML parser quirks, extra steps, hidden commands, or formatting cannot preserve PASS after any contracted file byte change because blob identity changes.
Every requested static check produces exactly one PASS, FAIL, or N/A result.
Non-applicable node-syntax is N/A, never PASS, and does not by itself fail the static phase.
Applicable node-syntax parses candidate JavaScript without running top-level code.
Invalid syntax fails while raw candidate source and diagnostics are not printed to operator-visible logs.
Exact candidate SHA mismatch or stale target fails before trusted check dispatch.
Registry, Risk Policy, executor, workflow, actor, run, attempt, Plan Lock, and target provenance are retained in evidence.
Static artifact is uploaded before the ruleset-required job returns static failure.
The implementation PR itself is not treated as proof of the newly added executor; post-merge failure and success canaries are required.
testPlan: Run Change Operations Tests including registry/executor unit and adversarial tests.
Require existing base-owned Change PR Gate and C3-1 Change Verification Evidence to pass on the implementation PR.
Perform exact-head adversarial review of registry transition, exact-blob contracts, node-syntax non-execution, provenance, logs, and artifact ordering before merge.

Failure canary: use an unknown command-like static check ID containing newline/bidi text; confirm trusted Static Evidence records explicit failure, operator logs contain no raw injected line/control, and the active ruleset rejects merge.

Contract canary: modify a contracted security-critical file while also changing candidate registry expectedBlob; confirm the base-owned registry wins and the required check fails, proving same-PR self-authorization is impossible.

Success canary: change a JavaScript file containing top-level code that would throw if executed; confirm node-syntax PASS, exact candidate SHA/workflow SHA/registry blob/executor blob/Risk Policy blob provenance, all required checks pass, and verificationState remains UNVERIFIED.
Close all canaries unmerged and reconfirm staging main remains the C3-2 merge commit and production main remains unchanged.
plan.promotionRisk: None. C3-2 is staging-only Change OS infrastructure and production must remain unchanged.
